topic: identifying unit fractions in area models (grades 2-3)
subtitle: Naming the unit fraction for one shaded part, checking that the parts really are equal, and comparing unit fractions drawn in same size shapes

problems.note: Rectangle cut into 4 equal parts, 1 part shaded.
Circle cut into 3 equal parts, 1 part shaded.
Square cut into 8 equal parts (2 rows of 4), 1 part shaded.

traps.desc: counted only the cut lines instead of the parts they make

problems.note: Two bars, both cut into 6 pieces: bar A equal, bar B unequal. Only A's shaded piece is a unit fraction.
One equal part is drawn away from the whole bar of 5 equal parts; name the strip's fraction of the bar.

traps.desc: named the piece by how many pieces are left in the bar instead of how many the whole was cut into

problems.note: Two same size rectangles, one cut into 3 equal parts and one into 6, each with 1 part shaded.
Three same size squares cut into 2, 8 and 4 equal parts; order the three shaded unit fractions smallest to largest.

problems.desc: Error analysis, open written explanation: a shape is cut into 3 pieces that are not the same size and a classmate calls the shaded piece one third. The child must explain why the name does not fit. Manual review.
